instance.finding_key: packages/notes/src/view/list-empty-bullet-plugin.ts::`ruler.at('lheading', ...)` is called without an `options.alt`, discarding whatever alt chain the installed markdown-it registers for `lheading`

finding.summary: `Ruler.at('lheading', ...)` is called without an `options.alt`, discarding whatever alt chain the installed markdown-it registers for `lheading`
finding.evidence: `md.block.ruler.at('lheading', lheadingRule);` at list-empty-bullet-plugin.ts:175 passes no options, while the very next `at()` call (:197-199) does pass `{ alt: ['paragraph','reference','blockquote'] }` precisely because, as the change's own lessons file records, `Ruler.at(name, fn, options)` REPLACES the rule's \`alt\` chain with \`options.alt || []\` (docs/tasks/active/20260724-notes-empty-bullet-setext-lessons.md:19). The author applied that lesson to `list` and not to `lheading`. In markdown-it 14.x's `parser_block` registry `lheading` is declared with no alt chain, so this is likely harmless today — but it is an unguarded assumption about a third-party private table, and if the pinned version (or a future bump) gives `lheading` any alt membership, it silently stops terminating paragraphs/blockquotes/references for consumers well outside this file. To confirm, check `node_modules/markdown-it/lib/parser_block.mjs` for the `lheading` entry's third element. Fix belongs on the new code: pass the upstream alt chain back explicitly, as was done for `list`.

decision.reason: I could not verify or refute the finding because the cited files are absent from my working directory, which holds only a 43-entry partial checkout (.materialized: "d7fea222a81170524e3e74bd41ac633ba21dfe95 43"). Glob for **/list-empty-bullet-plugin.ts, packages/**/*.ts, and **/notes/** all returned no matches; Grep for "lheading" across the entire cache returned zero hits; and no markdown-it install exists (**/parser_block* no match), so I could not inspect the lheading registry entry's third element as the finding requests. The only materialized content is agent/, hooks/, test/verify-entropy.test.mjs and top-level verify-*.mjs scripts, none of which touch markdown-it rulers. This absence is an environment/materialization gap, not evidence the code differs from the description, so `not-present` is unavailable. `pre-existing` is also unavailable: the authoritative changed-file list explicitly includes packages/notes/src/view/list-empty-bullet-plugin.ts. And `out-of-scope` does not apply on the rubric, since a call that silently discards an upstream alt chain and alters paragraph/blockquote/reference termination for consumers outside the file is exactly the blast-radius lane (behaviour change to a shared rule whose other consumers were not considered). Per the rule that uncertainty for any reason keeps the finding, it stays on the merge gate; a verifier with the full packages/notes tree and node_modules/markdown-it should re-check the two adjacent at() calls and the lheading alt entry.
